dev-scaffold: the start-up race is fixed and the acceptance tests discriminate, but the narrower monitor rule lets an agent read ~/.claude

Commit 5c96432 by the boss adds the template's test suite, model/effort settings, a narrower monitor rule for .claude/.ssh, and a fix for a gateway start-up race. Measured here with the real gateway, the real hook and real Claude Code sessions: main's gateway lost an agent's door in 7 of 1250 fresh-board starts, dev-scaffold's in 0 of 1250. tests/regress.sh passes (43 of 43), and each of the 7 acceptance tests fails on dev-scaffold and passes at the stack tip with the team's counts. The monitor rule now lets grep .claude through, but also lets through 6 commands the old rule paused; in a real agent session, wc -c ~/'.claude'/history.jsonl opened the user's Claude Code prompt history for reading (1,579,801 bytes) without a pause. The dev run (7 agents, 8 of 8 in 33.3 minutes) gets its page from the new report tool.

The race and the fix

Board.__init__ (gateway.py:121 at main) switches the board to WAL. On a new board that needs the database to itself; SQLite answers the losing thread "database is locked" without waiting out its 10 s timeout (in every failing start the Traceback is printed before the other agents' first answers), and the thread, which has no handler, dies.

Findings

  1. The narrower .claude rule lets an agent read the user's ~/.claude, without a pause. At main, any Bash command that mentioned .claude paused the team (\.claude\b). dev-scaffold's rule (hook.py:44 there, hook.py:55 at the tip) pauses only when .claude follows /, a space, =, (, <, > or the line start, and is followed by /, a space or the end. A quote, a brace or a variable breaks that: ~/'.claude'/x, ~/".claude/x", ~/{.claude,x}/x and X=.claude; cat ~/$X/x all pass the rule (hook matrix), where main paused all four. The sandbox does not cover the gap: mk_settings.py hides only ~/.claude/.credentials.json, projects and settings.json (CREDS, lines 15-17) and skips every dot-folder directly in the home directory (line 27). In a real Claude Code session with helper h1's real settings, wc -c ~/'.claude'/history.jsonl returned 1,579,801 bytes and ls of ~/.claude listed 28 entries; the monitor recorded pass and the auto-mode classifier did not object. history.jsonl holds the user's prompts from every project. Other files there (for example a settings backup) were not tried. The same command without quotes paused the team, as intended. template/harness/hook.py:55 and template/harness/mk_settings.py:15-17, 27
  2. dev-scaffold also deleted the board.db rule, which its commit message does not mention. main had \bboard\.db\b as a pausing rule (main hook.py:44). It is gone, so grep board.db x.py passes (wanted), and so do sqlite3 ../../state/board.db .dump and cat ../../state/board.db from a workspace. The remaining rule (hook.py:52 at the tip) matches <work dir name>/state, so a relative path never matches; ../../records/... and ../../harness/... already passed at main. Here the second layer holds: in the real session all three relative paths came back "No such file or directory". template/harness/hook.py:52 (the rule that remains)
  3. One false alarm is left: git log --grep=.claude still pauses the team. = is in the set of characters accepted before .claude (meant for --file=.claude/x), so any --opt=.claude pauses. template/harness/hook.py:55
  4. boss.sh trust reports "answered yes" without looking, and once the agent exited instead. It sends Down, waits 0.4 s, sends Enter, and prints "answered yes" unconditionally. For the sonnet session in the take the pane afterwards showed the cursor still on "No, exit" and "Claude Code didn't start because this folder isn't trusted"; boss.sh had printed "lead: answered yes". 1 of the 3 answers given in this demo. That the Down key arrived before the menu took input is my reading of the screen, not verified. In a team the agent's window would sit at a shell while the boss believes it started. template/harness/boss.sh:23-25
  5. The race is real but rare on a loaded host; the commit's "about 2 in 25" was not reproduced. Main's gateway lost an agent's thread in 7 of 1250 starts (0.6%) at host load 4.5 to 20, against 0 of 1250 for dev-scaffold's (one-sided Fisher exact p = 0.008 for the pooled counts). A 6-start dry run at load 0.3 lost one. Consequence for the suite: tests/regress.sh:65-72 starts the gateway 15 times (with 12 agents) and counts Tracebacks; at the 7-agent rate measured here that would catch the old bug in only 1-(1-p)^15 = 8% of runs (computed, not run; with 12 agents the rate is probably higher, not measured). template/harness/gateway.py:613-620, 666-672 (the fix at the tip)
  6. report.py: two legend swatches are drawn at the top of the page. The legend uses class="k act" and class="k gone"; .act and .gone are position:absolute for the timeline, so the "tool calls" swatch lands at (464, 8) and "removed" at the top right corner (measured in Chromium). Cosmetic. The done-lane labels also overlap when two statements land close together (msg and resume in the dev run). template/harness/report.py:408, 414 (and 242, 244)
  7. Some acceptance checks pass when the feature is absent. Each acceptance test as a whole fails on dev-scaffold, so the suite discriminates. Single refusal checks pass vacuously there: for example goal.sh's "an exploratory contract is refused" passes because from-goal.py does not exist. The pass counts on the dev-scaffold side (5 to 17 per test) are mostly such checks and plain prerequisites. tests/accept/goal.sh
  8. Reading the dev run's board "read-only" still changed one of its files. teamrun's state/board.db-shm (SQLite's WAL index) changed during the take; board.db, board.db-wal, the records and the repositories did not. A mode=ro open of a WAL database rewrites that index. Copying first (as done for report.py) avoids it; devrun_check.py read the original directly.

Not covered

  • The race at an idle host at scale: every batch ran while other demos kept the 2-CPU host at load 4.5 to 20.
  • Which other files in ~/.claude an agent can read (only history.jsonl's size and a listing were tried; no contents were read).
  • Whether the auto-mode classifier would stop such a read in a real team run with a less explicit prompt.
  • The effort level as the session reports it: the pane's status line is this host's custom statusline and shows only the model; the effort is shown by the argv.
  • tests/team/*.sh and tests/check.sh (stub-based; not proof here). The accept and regress tests also use stub tmux and claude; they are shown as the commit's own claim, run as written.
  • The dev run's live sessions: only its records were read.

Audit trail

One take (msg-scaf.cast, 753.6 s, 11 chapters), recorded with rec.sh and driven by take.sh; nothing typed by a person; no take discarded.

Before the take, off camera: race.sh 6+6 starts, regress.sh once (43/43) and hookmatrix.py once, to check the scripts. hookmatrix.py's expect column was written before that first run.

During the take, at about 01:30, sbxprobe.sh and accept.sh got one line each (exec > >(tee ...)) so that their output is also saved to a file; neither had started yet.

Off the take: interleaved before/after race batches (race/logs-ab1..3), the sonnet/low session rerun at 01:38 (the in-take one quit at the trust prompt), the dev run page screenshot, and the PNG rendering of pane captures with shoot.py --term.

Prompts answered for the user: harness/boss.sh trust answered Claude Code's folder-trust prompt three times, for the scratch workspaces mdl/opus/run/ws/lead and mdl/sonnet/run/ws/lead (twice). No other prompt was answered.

Claude Code sessions started: 4 (one claude -p probe at effort low with 7 tool calls; opus/xhigh lead for about 25 s; sonnet/low lead twice, about 30 s once and once quitting at the trust prompt). The panes showed 15.7K to 17.5K context each, so roughly 60K input tokens in all. Each was killed with its tmux session within a minute.

Every command printed by the probe session is a byte count or an error: no file contents from ~/.claude were read or recorded.

teamrun was only read (and copied with cp -a to devrun/); see the finding about board.db-shm. wt/stall and the repository were not modified (archives were made with git archive).

Secrets: the cast and this page were searched for API keys, tokens, .credentials, and e-mail addresses; none found, nothing masked.

Cleanup: every gateway started here was stopped by its own PID; the tmux sessions demo-msg-scaf and demo-msg-scaf2 and the rec servers were killed; tmux ls and ps show nothing of this page left running.
